revisions.summary: The voice keeps speaking across the swell before the drums return. I gave its quick ending light catches, brought out the recurring high reply over the drums, and restored the little word just before the late kick. (At 32.8 s the tail's last syllable falls 80 ms before the drum's return: the drum stands for both.)

points.text: Follow the stressed vowel into the much lighter tail.
The delayed high reply and the bright accent at the end answer the low drum.
The short word between the upper note and the kick has its own catch.

revisions.summary: From your marks and words. The upper figure you marked (two wide strokes, then six close ones, every bar) is now complete from the first bar to 17.3 s: every mark has a landing except the very first (0.08 s, too early for a ride to land). To keep it from being the only thing for 17 seconds: at first it is the line itself, with the call's stressed syllables giving some strokes their weight; from 6.2 s, where the voice stops, it rises alone; from 9 s, when the voice returns over the low entries, it goes on underneath, strokes shared with a word or a low entry keeping that weight and the others dropping to a whisper; its last bar rises into the swell.

points.text: The figure as the line, under the call.
The figure whispering under the voice and the low entries.
Its last bar rises into the swell.

revisions.summary: From your note: the quick voice before the second drum return is now followed syllable by syllable, light and rising into the drum, as before the first return (18.6–20.1 s).

points.text: Seven light syllables rising into the drum.

revisions.summary: The intention: Let the held call carry the rider forward at a walk. When the upper notes have two seconds to themselves, the rider lifts with them, then sinks under the returning voice. Both little strings of syllables draw the rider close to the ground. Out of each drum entrance comes a rolling stride, rising on the three low rebounds together. After the last kick the treble keeps hopping as the forward motion ebbs away.

The intention: Hang over the held call, then cross the exposed upper notes in a quicker, shallower sweep. When the singer comes back, settle closer to the ground and let the little upper notes brush past. The two quiet runs of syllables let the drums hit in clear space. After each return, start low and let the offbeat bass push the rider upward. Coast out on the bright notes after the last kick.

The intention: Airborne, then stamping. For the long opening the rider swings with the upper figure: the two wide strokes of every bar are two tall, slow arcs and the six close ones a low ripple along the line, and the swing changes with the voice: small and slow under the held call, wider and quicker when the figure is left alone at 6.2, hushed and low when the voice returns, and widening again into the swell. The quick voice before the drum is a light run gathering speed. Then the drum puts the foot down and the motion turns over: from 20.1 to the end the rider stays low and fast, stamping along the line on the quarters, with no tall arcs left, except the long syllable at 28.9, which is ridden like the run before the first drum and lands on the second downstroke at full weight.

The intention: Two halves, each with one figure per bar. In the long opening the rider swings with the upper figure: the two wide strokes of every bar are two tall slow arcs and the six close ones a low ripple along the line (Opus, whose ride shows this figure plainly, and an answer to your wish for something more than the same sounds for 17 seconds). The swing changes with the voice: small and slow under the held call, wider when the figure is left alone at 6.2, hushed under the returning voice, the figure there whispering a little more (Opus). The light runs of syllables before each drum downstroke are ridden as approved, the second like the first as you asked. In the drum half the figure turns into a surge: each downstroke lands low and the low rebounds push the rider up through the bar, once per bar (Sol, at whose ride the first downstroke lands hardest; Astra had the same rise). After the last kick the rider coasts out on the bright notes (Sol and Astra).
